en: I feel love, hey!
I feel love, love, hey!
Hey, see that girl far off,
I feel love, love, hey!
The cempedak fruit is outside the fence,
take a pole and please knock it down;
I am a child just learning,
if I am wrong please show me.
Pandan Island lies far out to sea,
Mount Daik has three peaks;
though the body crumbles in the earth,
a good deed is still remembered.
Two, three cats are running;
none is like the striped cat.
Two, three I could find;
none is like my one beloved.
Golden bananas taken on a voyage,
one ripens on top of a chest;
a debt of gold can be repaid,
a debt of kindness is carried to the grave.
notes: The verses are pantun, the Malay quatrain: the first two lines give an image, the last two the message, tied to the image by rhyme rather than sense. Any pantun can be sung to the tune between the choruses.
Stanza 4: abang (here "my one beloved") is literally "elder brother", the usual word for a sweetheart in Malay songs.
